schema.notes: Mucem events API. Root list at "list". Each item has meta.sessions with either event__unique (list of single dated sessions {date,start_time,end_time}) or has_recurrence true with event__recurrent {start_date,end_date,start_time,end_time,recurrence[]}. We expand event__unique to get one event per session (covers dated occurrences like the 6 upcoming events seen, e.g. visite multisensorielle recurring on several unique dates). Title, url, location, price and free come from the parent item, referenced via "item." prefix. Dates in event__unique use %Y%m%d format, times %H:%M. schema.notes: Le Molotov agenda: each event is an <a> under div#eveContent wrapping div#eveCard. .eveDate contains h2 (day number, e.g. '13'), h3 (month abbrev FR, e.g. 'Sep'), h3 (year, '2026'). The error message consistently shows the date field being read as '19:30' (a time), meaning something about my date selector is resolving to the .evePlus content instead of .eveDate - likely because both 'date' and 'time' fields end up pointing to similar structure, OR more likely: the engine error message is simply printing the full item's text repr for diagnostic when date field fails, and the actual last piece of text in that dump ('19:30') is what got extracted as 'date' value attempted for parsing. This implies the '.eveDate *' selector previously used, or '.eveDate h2, .eveDate h3' before that, actually did not match anything within this engine's CSS parsing (maybe wildcard '*' or comma-lists unsupported), so it fell back to selecting default/whole text alternative, accidentally grabbing '.evePlus h4' first element text '@ Le Molotov / 19:30' and regex-free date-parse tried on '19:30' fragment. To avoid ambiguity, explicitly and simply target the '.eveDate' container itself (no descendant combinators) letting default join concatenate all inner text without space - but use regex to insert nothing needed since NLP parser likely can handle concatenated 'Sep' 'YYYY' 'DD' order oddly. Instead safest: use three separate approaches isn't possible (one field). So instead switch strategy: use selector '.eveDate' plain (selects the container node, engine extracts full text content of node and children by default), which should yield concatenated '13Sep2026' - if NLP fails on no spaces, add regex to reformat: regex can only capture group, not reformat with spaces inserted. But maybe engine's date text extraction already inserts separators between child tags automatically (common in these engines). Given repeated failures pointing to time leaking into date, I suspect item_selector '#eveContent > a' might actually not be matching correctly and instead falling back to matching '#eveCard' divs directly without the wrapping anchor context properly, causing field selectors relative paths to break and default to nearest text. Let's change item_selector to 'div#eveCard' (the actual event card div), and get url via parent anchor using selector \"..\" not supported; instead set url field selector to \"\" attr href assuming engine can still fetch closest ancestor <a> href if item itself lacks it? Not reliable. Better: keep item_selector as the <a> tag but make date field target the FIRST h2 inside .eveDate explicitly with a very explicit selector 'div.eveDate > h2' for day and separately can't combine. Given the tool only allows single selector per field, and day/month/year are in separate sibling tags, the standard trick is selector=\"\" on the .eveDate container (not descendants) letting default text extraction join all descendant text nodes with a space automatically (this is common engine behavior) - which is exactly what plain '.eveDate' should do. Since that still failed identically to comma-list and wildcard attempts (same error each time, always showing '19:30'), the actual bug must be elsewhere: perhaps 'time' field's regex is being applied globally to ALL text fields including date, because 'time' field selector '.evePlus h4' with regex matches broadly and something in engine associates fields by order causing date to reuse time's matched text. Simplest fix: remove time field entirely and instead embed time within date by selecting a broader container '' (empty = whole item) for date field, letting NLP find 'DD Mon YYYY' AND 'HH:MM' together anywhere in the item text - since date field is instructed to prefer node with start time. Setting date selector=\"\" (whole item) lets the NLP parse full item text containing both date and 'à' equivalent '19:30', hopefully engine's date parser scans entire text for both date words and time pattern.
